title: Envelope Encryption & Key Policies with AWS KMS
goal: Goal: Create a Customer Managed Key (CMK) and enforce cryptographic access control using KMS Key Policies and Envelope Encryption.

concepts.title: KMS Key Policies
concepts.body: The primary access control mechanism for KMS keys. Unlike S3 or IAM policies, IAM policies alone cannot grant access to a KMS key unless the KMS Key Policy explicitly permits the account/role.

concepts.title: Envelope Encryption
concepts.body: Encrypting plaintext data with a Data Key locally, and then encrypting the Data Key under a master KMS Key (CMK). Essential for encrypting datasets larger than 4 KB.

concepts.title: Data Keys vs KMS Master Keys
concepts.body: KMS CMK: Never leaves the HSM hardware; encrypts/decrypts up to 4 KB. Data Key: Generated by KMS; used locally by your application to encrypt large payload data.

concepts.title: Automatic Key Rotation
concepts.body: AWS KMS automatically rotates Customer Managed Keys every 365 days, retaining old key versions so existing encrypted data can still be decrypted seamlessly.

concepts.title: KMS Key Types & Rotation Matrix
concepts.body: Key TypeManaged ByRotation OptionsKey Policy ModificationAWS Managed Key (e.g. `aws/s3`)AWS ServicesAutomatic every 3 years (Fixed)No (Read-only policy)Customer Managed Key (CMK)Customer (You)Optional automatic annual (365 days) rotationYes (Full policy customization)AWS Owned KeyAWS InternalManaged internally by AWSNo access

whyItMatters: This matters because KMS Key Policies act as the primary access boundary for keys, and envelope encryption allows encrypting data > 4 KB locally using Data Keys on SAA-C03.
costWarning: KMS key, request, rotation and connected-service charges may apply.

consoleSteps.title: Create a Symmetric Customer Managed Key (CMK)

instructions.text: Open AWS KMS Console -> Click Customer managed keys in left navigation -> Click Create key.
Select Key type Symmetric -> Select Key usage Encrypt and decrypt -> Click Next.
Set Alias to alias/saa-kms-app-key and Description to App master key for envelope encryption.
Click Next.

consoleSteps.note: Creates a symmetric 256-bit AES Customer Managed Key stored in AWS HSM hardware.

consoleSteps.title: Define Restrictive KMS Key Policy and Enable Automatic Rotation

instructions.text: Under Key administrators, select your IAM admin user.
Under Key usage permissions, select your application IAM role or user.
Check Automatically rotate this KMS key every year.
Review autogenerated JSON Key Policy ensuring `kms:Decrypt` and `kms:GenerateDataKey` are granted strictly to target IAM principals.
Click Finish.

consoleSteps.note: Key policies define who can manage and use the key independently of IAM policies.

consoleSteps.title: Simulate Envelope Encryption and Generate Data Key

instructions.text: Open terminal and execute Data Key generation: aws kms generate-data-key --key-id alias/saa-kms-app-key --key-spec AES_256 --region us-east-1.
Inspect output JSON containing Plaintext (for local payload encryption) and CiphertextBlob (encrypted Data Key to store alongside payload).
Demonstrate zeroing out the Plaintext key in local memory after payload encryption completes.

consoleSteps.note: Envelope encryption protects payloads > 4 KB by storing encrypted Data Keys with payload data.

consoleSteps.title: Tear down lab resources

instructions.text: Delete KMS alias alias/saa-kms-app-key.
Select CMK -> Choose Key actions -> Click Schedule key deletion.
Set waiting period to 7 days -> Click Schedule deletion.

consoleSteps.warning: KMS keys have a mandatory 7 to 30 day deletion waiting period before permanent destruction.

cheatSheet.title: KMS Key Policies
cheatSheet.body: Primary access control mechanism for KMS. IAM policies cannot grant access without Key Policy permission.

cheatSheet.title: Envelope Encryption
cheatSheet.body: Payload > 4 KB encrypted locally with Data Key; Data Key encrypted under KMS Master Key.

cheatSheet.title: Key Rotation
cheatSheet.body: Automatic annual rotation retains old key versions for seamless decryption of historical data.

troubleshooting.title: KMS Access Denied Despite Admin IAM Policy
troubleshooting.body: IAM Policies alone are insufficient for KMS. The KMS Key Policy MUST explicitly delegate access to the root account or specific IAM user/role.

examTraps.title: 4 KB Direct Payload Limit Trap
examTraps.body: AWS KMS `kms:Encrypt` API cannot directly encrypt payloads larger than **4 KB (4096 bytes)**. For larger files, choose Envelope Encryption (GenerateDataKey).

examTips.text: SAA-C03: Master AWS KMS concepts and data security patterns in AWS KMS.

memoryHook: Key Policy = Mandatory KMS Access Boundary | Envelope Encryption = Data Key for Payload > 4 KB

title: Encrypted S3 Bucket Policies & SSE-KMS Cross-Account Sharing
goal: Goal: Share an encrypted S3 bucket and its KMS-encrypted objects with an external AWS account using cross-account policies.

concepts.title: Dual Policy Requirement for SSE-KMS
concepts.body: Accessing SSE-KMS encrypted S3 objects across AWS accounts requires explicit permissions in BOTH the S3 Bucket Policy AND the KMS Key Policy.

concepts.title: SSE-S3 vs SSE-KMS Cross-Account
concepts.body: SSE-S3 (AES-256): Managed by S3; sharing requires S3 Bucket Policy permission only. SSE-KMS: Managed by KMS; sharing requires S3 Bucket Policy AND KMS Key Policy permissions.

concepts.title: KMS Key Policy Trust Statement
concepts.body: The KMS Key Policy in Account A must grant `kms:Decrypt`, `kms:Encrypt`, and `kms:GenerateDataKey` to Account B's root or specific IAM role ARN.

concepts.title: S3 Bucket Policy Trust Statement
concepts.body: The S3 Bucket Policy in Account A must grant `s3:GetObject` and `s3:PutObject` to Account B's IAM principal.

concepts.title: SSE-S3 vs SSE-KMS Cross-Account Access Comparison Matrix
concepts.body: Encryption TypeKey ManagerRequired Policy Changes for Cross-Account SharingSSE-S3 (AES-256)Amazon S3 Managed KeysS3 Bucket Policy ONLY (Grant `s3:GetObject` to Account B)SSE-KMS (aws/s3)AWS Managed KMS KeyNOT SUPPORTED for Cross-Account (AWS Managed Keys cannot be shared)SSE-KMS (CMK)Customer Managed KeyDUAL POLICY REQUIRED: S3 Bucket Policy AND KMS Key Policy

whyItMatters: This matters because accessing SSE-KMS encrypted objects across accounts requires explicit permission in both the S3 Bucket Policy AND the KMS Key Policy on SAA-C03.
costWarning: KMS key, request, rotation and connected-service charges may apply.

consoleSteps.title: Create S3 Bucket with SSE-KMS Default Encryption

instructions.text: Open Amazon S3 Console in Account A -> Click Create bucket.
Set Bucket name to saa-cross-account-kms-[account-id] in us-east-1.
Under Default encryption, select Server-side encryption with AWS Key Management Service keys (SSE-KMS).
Select your Customer Managed Key alias/saa-kms-app-key.
Click Create bucket.

consoleSteps.note: Enforces SSE-KMS default encryption on all uploaded objects.

consoleSteps.title: Update KMS Key Policy to Trust External Account B

instructions.text: Open AWS KMS Console in Account A -> Select Customer Managed Key alias/saa-kms-app-key.
Choose Key policy tab -> Click Edit.
Add Statement granting kms:Decrypt, kms:Encrypt, and kms:GenerateDataKey to Principal arn:aws:iam::222222222222:root.
Click Save changes.

consoleSteps.note: KMS Key Policy must explicitly trust Account B; default KMS policies deny external access.

consoleSteps.title: Update S3 Bucket Policy to Trust External Account B

instructions.text: Open Amazon S3 Console -> Select saa-cross-account-kms-[account-id].
Choose Permissions tab -> Click Edit bucket policy.
Add Statement granting s3:GetObject and s3:PutObject to Principal arn:aws:iam::222222222222:root.
Click Save changes.

consoleSteps.note: S3 Bucket Policy grants bucket level access to Account B.

consoleSteps.title: Verify Cross-Account Read/Write from Account B

instructions.text: Switch credentials to Account B IAM role.
Upload test object: aws s3 cp file.txt s3://saa-cross-account-kms-111111111111/file.txt --region us-east-1.
Download test object: aws s3 cp s3://saa-cross-account-kms-111111111111/file.txt downloaded.txt --region us-east-1.
Confirm successful read and write operation.

consoleSteps.note: Confirms dual policy authorization works seamlessly across accounts.

instructions.text: Empty and delete S3 bucket saa-cross-account-kms-[account-id].

cheatSheet.title: Dual Policy Requirement
cheatSheet.body: Cross-account SSE-KMS access requires explicit permissions in BOTH S3 Bucket Policy and KMS Key Policy.

cheatSheet.title: AWS Managed KMS Keys Cannot Be Shared
cheatSheet.body: Default AWS Managed Keys (`aws/s3`) cannot be shared across accounts. You MUST use a **Customer Managed Key (CMK)**.

cheatSheet.title: SSE-S3 vs SSE-KMS
cheatSheet.body: SSE-S3 requires S3 Bucket Policy sharing only; SSE-KMS requires S3 Bucket Policy + KMS Key Policy sharing.

troubleshooting.title: Access Denied on Cross-Account GetObject

examTraps.title: AWS Managed Key Sharing Trap
examTraps.body: You CANNOT share S3 objects encrypted with the default `aws/s3` AWS Managed Key across accounts. You MUST re-encrypt objects using a Customer Managed Key (CMK).

examTips.text: SAA-C03: Master AWS KMS concepts and data security patterns in AWS KMS.

title: Encrypting Existing Unencrypted EBS Volumes & AMIs
goal: Goal: Migrate an unencrypted EC2 block storage volume to an encrypted EBS volume without data loss using the mandatory SAA-C03 snapshot migration pattern.

concepts.title: No Direct In-Place Volume Encryption
concepts.body: You CANNOT directly encrypt an existing unencrypted EBS volume in-place. You must follow the mandatory 4-step migration workflow.

concepts.title: The Mandatory SAA-C03 EBS Encryption Workflow
concepts.body: Step 1: Create Snapshot of unencrypted volume. Step 2: Copy Snapshot while checking Enable Encryption with a KMS key. Step 3: Create encrypted volume or AMI from copied snapshot. Step 4: Attach encrypted volume / launch replacement instance.

concepts.title: EBS Default Encryption
concepts.body: Region-level account setting that automatically encrypts all newly created EBS volumes and snapshot copies using a specified KMS key.

concepts.title: KMS Key Selection during Snapshot Copy
concepts.body: During the snapshot copy operation, you can select the default `aws/ebs` key or a custom Customer Managed Key (CMK).

concepts.title: EBS Encryption Workflow Matrix
concepts.body: EBS Resource StateDirect Action Allowed?Required Workaround / Migration PathExisting Unencrypted EBS VolumeNo in-place encryptionSnapshot -> Copy Snapshot with Encryption -> Create VolumeExisting Unencrypted AMINo in-place encryptionCopy AMI with Encryption -> Launch Encrypted EC2 InstanceNew EBS Volume CreationYes (Enable encryption)Check `Encrypt this volume` during creationNew EC2 Launch (EBS Default)Yes (Account setting)Enable `EBS default encryption` in EC2 region settings

whyItMatters: This matters because you cannot directly encrypt an existing unencrypted EBS volume in-place. The mandatory SAA-C03 pattern is: Snapshot -> Copy Snapshot with Encryption -> Create Volume/AMI.
costWarning: KMS key, request, rotation and connected-service charges may apply.

consoleSteps.title: Set up the lab user and permissions

instructions.text: Sign in to the AWS Management Console.
Sign in to the AWS Management Console using an IAM user or lab role with appropriate permissions.
Sign in to the AWS Management Console using an IAM user or lab role with appropriate permissions.
For least privilege, use the grouped permissions below.

consoleSteps.note: Identity check: sts:GetCallerIdentity EC2 / EBS permissions: ec2:CreateSnapshot, ec2:CopySnapshot, ec2:CreateVolume, ec2:RunInstances Cleanup: ec2:DeleteSnapshot, ec2:DeleteVolume, ec2:TerminateInstances
consoleSteps.warning: Do not leave broad admin access or long-term access keys in real company accounts.

consoleSteps.title: Launch Unencrypted EC2 Instance and Create Unencrypted Snapshot

instructions.text: Open Amazon EC2 Console -> Click Launch instance (Ensure volume encryption is disabled).
Stop the instance once running to ensure file system consistency.
Open Volumes -> Select unencrypted root volume -> Click Actions -> Choose Create snapshot.
Set Description to snap-unencrypted-source -> Click Create snapshot.

consoleSteps.note: Stopping the instance before snapshot creation prevents file system corruption.

consoleSteps.title: Copy Snapshot and Enable KMS Encryption

instructions.text: Open Snapshots -> Select snap-unencrypted-source -> Click Actions -> Choose Copy snapshot.
Under Encryption, check Encrypt this snapshot.
Select KMS key aws/ebs (or Customer Managed Key alias/saa-kms-app-key).
Set Description to snap-kms-encrypted-copy -> Click Copy snapshot.

consoleSteps.note: The copy operation re-encrypts all data blocks under the target KMS key.

consoleSteps.title: Create Encrypted Volume or AMI from Encrypted Snapshot

instructions.text: Select snap-kms-encrypted-copy -> Click Actions -> Choose Create volume from snapshot (or Create image from snapshot).
Verify volume configuration displays Encrypted: Yes.
Click Create volume.

consoleSteps.note: Creates a new encrypted EBS block device pre-populated with original data.

consoleSteps.title: Attach Encrypted Volume and Launch Replacement Instance

instructions.text: Attach the newly created encrypted volume to your replacement EC2 instance.
Start instance and confirm OS boots cleanly with all original files intact.
Review EBS Default Encryption setting.

consoleSteps.note: Completes the zero-data-loss volume encryption migration.

consoleSteps.title: Tear down lab resources

instructions.text: Terminate EC2 instances.
Delete test volumes and snapshots snap-unencrypted-source and snap-kms-encrypted-copy.

consoleSteps.warning: Delete snapshots and terminated volumes to free up account storage.

cheatSheet.title: No In-Place EBS Encryption
cheatSheet.body: You CANNOT encrypt an existing unencrypted volume directly. Must use Snapshot -> Copy with Encryption -> Create Volume.

cheatSheet.title: 4-Step Migration Pattern
cheatSheet.body: 1. Snapshot unencrypted volume. 2. Copy snapshot + enable KMS encryption. 3. Create volume/AMI from encrypted snapshot. 4. Attach to replacement instance.

cheatSheet.title: EBS Default Encryption
cheatSheet.body: Enabling EBS default encryption automatically encrypts all new volumes and snapshot copies in the region.

troubleshooting.title: Cannot Attach Volume to Instance
troubleshooting.body: Ensure the newly created encrypted volume resides in the EXACT same Availability Zone (e.g. `us-east-1a`) as the EC2 instance.

examTraps.title: In-Place Encryption Trap
examTraps.body: If an exam question asks how to encrypt an existing unencrypted EBS volume, do NOT select 'Modify volume settings to enable encryption'. Select Snapshot -> Copy Snapshot with Encryption -> Create Volume.

examTips.text: SAA-C03: Master AWS KMS concepts and data security patterns in AWS KMS.

memoryHook: EBS Encryption = Snapshot -> Copy + Encrypt -> Volume

title: Transport Layer Security (TLS/SSL) with ACM & ALB
goal: Goal: Secure application endpoints in transit using public SSL/TLS certificates issued by AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) and attached to an ALB.

concepts.title: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) Scope
concepts.body: ALB / API Gateway / App Runner: ACM certificates must be requested in the SAME Region as the resource. CloudFront Distributions: ACM certificates MUST be requested in us-east-1 (N. Virginia).

concepts.title: ALB HTTPS Redirection
concepts.body: ALB listeners can automatically redirect unencrypted HTTP (port 80) requests to encrypted HTTPS (port 443) using HTTP status code 301 (Moved Permanently).

concepts.title: Security Policies & TLS 1.3
concepts.body: ALB HTTPS listeners evaluate Security Policies defining supported TLS versions and cipher suites (e.g. `ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06`).

concepts.title: SSL Offloading / Termination
concepts.body: The ALB decrypts HTTPS traffic at the load balancer layer, offloading CPU cryptographic processing from backend EC2 instances.

concepts.title: ACM Certificate Scope & Target Comparison Matrix
concepts.body: Target ResourceMandatory ACM Certificate RegionSSL Termination LocationApplication Load Balancer (ALB)Same Region as the ALB (e.g., us-east-1)Load Balancer Layer (ALB Listener)Amazon CloudFront Distributionus-east-1 (N. Virginia) ONLYGlobal Edge LocationsAmazon API Gateway Custom DomainSame Region as the API GatewayAPI Gateway Edge / Regional Endpoint

whyItMatters: This matters because regional scope of ACM certificates (e.g. CloudFront requires us-east-1 while ALBs use local region certificates) and HTTP to HTTPS redirects are heavily tested on SAA-C03.
costWarning: KMS key, request, rotation and connected-service charges may apply.

consoleSteps.title: Request Public ACM Certificate in Local ALB Region

instructions.text: Open AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) Console in us-east-1.
Click Request certificate -> Select Request a public certificate.
Set Domain name to app.example.com.
Select Validation method DNS validation -> Click Request.
Complete DNS validation in Route 53 until status shows Issued.

consoleSteps.note: ALB certificates MUST be requested in the same Region as the ALB.

consoleSteps.title: Configure HTTPS Port 443 Listener on ALB

instructions.text: Open EC2 Console -> Choose Load Balancers -> Select your ALB.
Choose Listeners tab -> Click Add listener.
Set Protocol:Port to HTTPS:443.
Set Default action to Forward to target group.
Under Security policy, select ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06.
Under Default SSL/TLS certificate, select your issued ACM certificate.
Click Add listener.

consoleSteps.note: Enables encrypted TLS 1.3 transport to the ALB endpoint.

consoleSteps.title: Configure HTTP Port 80 Automatic HTTPS Redirect Rule

instructions.text: In Listeners tab, click Add listener (or edit existing HTTP:80 listener).
Set Protocol:Port to HTTP:80.
Set Default action to Redirect to URL.
Select HTTPS on Port 443 with status code HTTP 301 (Moved Permanently).
Click Add listener.

consoleSteps.note: Forces all unencrypted HTTP traffic to redirect to secure HTTPS.

consoleSteps.title: Verify TLS Handshake and Redirection

instructions.text: Test HTTP redirect: curl -I http:/// (confirm HTTP/1.1 301 Moved Permanently with Location header pointing to HTTPS).
Test HTTPS handshake: curl -vI https:/// (confirm TLS 1.3 handshake succeeds).

consoleSteps.note: Validates redirection and TLS termination at the load balancer.

instructions.text: Delete ALB listeners and load balancer.
Delete target group.
Delete ACM certificate.

title: KMS key: only one role can use it
goal: Goal: Create a KMS key where only one IAM role can encrypt/decrypt, then prove a non-role principal fails and the role succeeds.

concepts.title: Least privilege
concepts.body: Grant only the exact action, resource, and principal needed.

concepts.title: Policy evaluation
concepts.body: AWS starts with implicit deny; explicit deny always wins.

concepts.title: Positive test
concepts.body: Proves the intended access works.

concepts.title: Negative test
concepts.body: Proves unintended access is blocked.

concepts.title: ARN accuracy
concepts.body: Most IAM labs fail because the ARN or principal is wrong.

concepts.title: Cleanup order
concepts.body: Delete dependent resources before roles, users, policies, and buckets.

whyItMatters: This lab makes IAM behaviour visible. You build a small setup, test both allowed and denied paths, then remove everything in dependency order.
costWarning: KMS key, request, rotation and connected-service charges may apply.

consoleSteps.title: Create the role first

instructions.text: IAM → Roles → Create role.
Trusted entity: AWS service. Use case: EC2.
Role name: AppEncryptionRole.
Copy the role ARN.

consoleSteps.warning: The role must exist before you reference it in the KMS key policy.

consoleSteps.title: Create the KMS key

instructions.text: KMS → Customer managed keys → Create key.
Choose symmetric, encrypt/decrypt.
Continue to key policy.

consoleSteps.title: Set strict key policy

instructions.text: Switch to JSON policy editor.
Replace ACCOUNT_ID and ROLE_ARN_HERE.

consoleSteps.title: Create alias and finish

instructions.text: Alias: alias/app-encryption.
Create the key.

consoleSteps.title: Fail test as no-permission user

instructions.text: Create IAM user no-kms-user with no permissions.
Create access keys and configure profile no-kms.
Try to encrypt.

consoleSteps.note: Expected: AccessDeniedException.

consoleSteps.title: Pass test from EC2 with role

instructions.text: Launch or use a small Linux EC2 instance.
Attach role AppEncryptionRole.
Run encrypt/decrypt from the instance.

consoleSteps.note: Expected: hello-from-ec2 is printed.

consoleSteps.title: Tear down

instructions.text: Terminate the EC2 test instance.
Schedule KMS key deletion.
Delete alias, no-kms user, role, and instance profile.

commands.text:
cat > trust-ec2.json <<'JSON'
{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"Service":"ec2.amazonaws.com"},"Action":"sts:AssumeRole"}]}
JSON
aws iam create-role --role-name AppEncryptionRole --assume-role-policy-document file://trust-ec2.json
aws iam create-instance-profile --instance-profile-name AppEncryptionRole
aws iam add-role-to-instance-profile --instance-profile-name AppEncryptionRole --role-name AppEncryptionRole

ACCOUNT_ID=$(aws sts get-caller-identity --query Account --output text)
ROLE_ARN=$(aws iam get-role --role-name AppEncryptionRole --query Role.Arn --output text)
echo "$ACCOUNT_ID $ROLE_ARN"

# Create kms-key-policy.json from the console policy, replacing ACCOUNT_ID and ROLE_ARN_HERE
KEY_ID=$(aws kms create-key --description "KMS key for AppEncryptionRole only lab" --policy file://kms-key-policy.json --query KeyMetadata.KeyId --output text)
aws kms create-alias --alias-name alias/app-encryption --target-key-id "$KEY_ID"

cliSteps.title: Create no-KMS user and prove deny

commands.text:
aws iam create-user --user-name no-kms-user
aws iam create-access-key --user-name no-kms-user
aws configure set aws_access_key_id NO_KMS_ACCESS_KEY_ID --profile no-kms
aws configure set aws_secret_access_key NO_KMS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY --profile no-kms
aws configure set region eu-west-2 --profile no-kms
echo "hello-kms" > plain.txt
aws kms encrypt --key-id alias/app-encryption --plaintext fileb://plain.txt --profile no-kms

cliSteps.title: Verify alias and tear down

commands.text:
aws kms list-aliases --query "Aliases[?AliasName=='alias/app-encryption']"
aws kms delete-alias --alias-name alias/app-encryption
aws kms schedule-key-deletion --key-id "$KEY_ID" --pending-window-in-days 7
AKID=$(aws iam list-access-keys --user-name no-kms-user --query "AccessKeyMetadata[0].AccessKeyId" --output text)
aws iam delete-access-key --user-name no-kms-user --access-key-id "$AKID"
aws iam delete-user --user-name no-kms-user
aws iam remove-role-from-instance-profile --instance-profile-name AppEncryptionRole --role-name AppEncryptionRole
aws iam delete-instance-profile --instance-profile-name AppEncryptionRole
aws iam delete-role --role-name AppEncryptionRole

title: Automated Password Rotation with Secrets Manager vs SSM Parameter Store
goal: Goal: Securely store application credentials and configure automated 30-day password rotation using AWS Secrets Manager, and contrast with SSM Parameter Store.

concepts.title: AWS Secrets Manager
concepts.body: Designed specifically for sensitive credentials (database passwords, API keys). Features built-in automated rotation via Lambda, native integration with RDS/Redshift, cross-region secret replication, and random password generation.

concepts.title: AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store
concepts.body: Lightweight, low-cost key-value store for application configuration parameters and secrets (`String`, `StringList`, `SecureString` encrypted with KMS). Does NOT support built-in automated rotation.

concepts.title: Automated Rotation Architecture
concepts.body: Secrets Manager invokes a Lambda function to update credentials inside the database first, and then updates the secret version in Secrets Manager.

concepts.title: SecureString Parameters
concepts.body: Parameter Store parameters encrypted using a KMS key. Free for standard parameters; ideal for configuration settings.

concepts.title: Secrets Manager vs SSM Parameter Store Decision Matrix
concepts.body: FeatureAWS Secrets ManagerAWS Systems Manager Parameter StorePrimary PurposeDatabase credentials, API keys, OAuth tokensGeneral app configuration, feature flags, license keysAutomated RotationNative Built-In (via AWS Lambda)No built-in rotation (Requires custom EventBridge + Lambda)RDS / Redshift IntegrationNative automated password rotation templatesManual script managementCross-Region ReplicationBuilt-in cross-region secret replicationManual replication or EventBridge synchronizationCost Profile$0.40 per secret per monthFree (Standard parameters) / $0.05 per Advanced parameter

whyItMatters: This matters because choosing Secrets Manager (automated rotation, RDS integration, cross-region replication) vs Parameter Store (low-cost hierarchical config storage) is a major SAA-C03 topic.
costWarning: Secrets Manager secret storage, API request, rotation Lambda and replication charges may apply.

cheatSheet.title: SSM Parameter Store

title: PII Scanning & Sensitive Data Discovery with Amazon Macie
goal: Goal: Automatically scan S3 buckets to discover exposed Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and credit card data using Amazon Macie.

concepts.title: Amazon Macie Overview
concepts.body: Data security and privacy service that uses machine learning and pattern matching to discover, classify, and protect sensitive data stored in Amazon S3.

concepts.title: Sensitive Data Discovery Jobs
concepts.body: Automated or on-demand scanning jobs targeting specified S3 buckets to inspect file contents (CSV, JSON, PDF, DOCX) for PII.

concepts.title: Types of Detectable PII Data
concepts.body: Social Security Numbers (SSN), Credit Card Numbers, Driver's License Numbers, Passport Numbers, Bank Account Details, and custom regex data types.

concepts.title: EventBridge Alert Integration
concepts.body: Macie publishes classification findings to Amazon EventBridge, allowing automated alerts or Lambda remediation functions to restrict bucket access.

concepts.title: Macie vs GuardDuty vs Inspector Comparison Matrix
concepts.body: Security ServicePrimary TargetDetection CapabilitiesAmazon MacieAmazon S3 BucketsDiscovers PII & sensitive data (SSNs, Credit Cards) stored in S3Amazon GuardDutyAWS Account / VPC / EKSDiscovers threats & malicious behavior (Compromised keys, C2 traffic)Amazon InspectorEC2 Instances, ECR Images, LambdaDiscovers software vulnerabilities (CVEs) & network exposure

whyItMatters: This matters because using Amazon Macie to discover exposed PII and sensitive data stored in S3 vs. GuardDuty for threat detection vs. Inspector for software CVEs is a high-frequency SAA-C03 question.
costWarning: Macie inventory, automated discovery and sensitive-data inspection charges may apply.

title: Intelligent Threat Detection with Amazon GuardDuty & Auto-Remediation
goal: Goal: Detect unauthorized API calls, compromised EC2 instances, or malicious IAM activity using Amazon GuardDuty and trigger automated EventBridge remediation.

concepts.title: Amazon GuardDuty Overview
concepts.body: Intelligent threat detection service that continuously monitors AWS accounts and workloads for malicious activity and unauthorized behavior.

concepts.title: GuardDuty Data Sources
concepts.body: Analyzes primary data sources without agent installation: AWS CloudTrail Event Logs, VPC Flow Logs, DNS Logs, plus optional S3 Data Events, EKS Audit Logs, and RDS Protection.

concepts.title: Automated Security Remediation
concepts.body: GuardDuty emits findings to EventBridge in real time. EventBridge rules trigger Lambda functions to isolate compromised EC2 Security Groups or revoke compromised IAM access keys.

concepts.title: GuardDuty vs Amazon Inspector
concepts.body: GuardDuty: Continuous threat detection analyzing log streams for active attacks. Inspector: Vulnerability scanning engine for EC2/ECR software CVEs and network reachability.

concepts.title: Security & Threat Detection Master Decision Matrix
concepts.body: AWS Security ServiceData Inputs AnalyzedPrimary Security ObjectiveAmazon GuardDutyCloudTrail Logs, VPC Flow Logs, DNS Logs, S3 LogsDetect active threats & compromised resourcesAmazon InspectorEC2 OS agent / ECR container imagesDetect software vulnerabilities (CVEs) & open portsAmazon MacieAmazon S3 Bucket object contentsDiscover unencrypted PII & sensitive dataAWS WAFHTTP/HTTPS requests at CloudFront / ALB / API GatewayBlock OWASP Top 10 web exploits & HTTP floods

whyItMatters: This matters because understanding GuardDuty (continuous threat detection using CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, DNS logs) vs Inspector (software vulnerability scanning) is a core SAA-C03 scenario.

values.label: Data Sources
values.value: CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, DNS Logs
